genes.name: centrosymmetric
genes.hypothesis: Building the set from antipodal pairs about the cube centre halves the search space, and the published records for n = 13 to 16 have exactly this symmetry (those for n >= 17 do not).
genes.predicted: +1 to +2 points for n >= 14, little or nothing for n <= 10
genes.author: seed

genes.name: lookahead
genes.hypothesis: When refilling, placing the free point that blocks the fewest other free points (best of lookahead_m samples) packs more points than placing a random one.
genes.predicted: +0.5 points at equal CPU time, more on large n where free lists are longer
genes.author: seed

genes.name: guided_ruin
genes.hypothesis: Aiming the ruin at a grid point blocked by a single sphere (remove one of that sphere's four members, insert the point first) makes every step a real exchange instead of a mostly futile random removal.
genes.predicted: +0.5 to +1 point at equal CPU time
genes.author: seed

genes.name: ruin_max
genes.hypothesis: Each step removes 1..ruin_max points (pairs when centrosymmetric); larger ruins escape deeper local optima but cost more per step.
genes.author: seed

genes.name: accept_worse_prob
genes.hypothesis: Probability of accepting a refill that is one unit smaller than the current set; a little downhill movement keeps the search from freezing on a plateau.
genes.author: seed

genes.name: patience
genes.hypothesis: Steps without a new best before a kick; too small never finishes polishing, too large wastes time in a dead basin.
genes.author: seed

genes.name: kick_fraction
genes.hypothesis: Fraction of the set removed by a kick; 1.0 is a full restart.
genes.author: seed

genes.name: lookahead_m
genes.hypothesis: Number of free points sampled per placement when lookahead is on; each sample costs one pass over all member triples.
genes.author: seed

genes.name: multi_recreate
genes.hypothesis: Each ruin costs a full pass over the incidence records and the grid while a tentative refill is cheap, so refilling the same hole multi_recreate_m times and keeping the largest refill (ties: the one with the most new points) gets several search attempts, and more real plateau moves, per expensive ruin.
genes.predicted: +0.3 to +0.7 points at equal CPU time on n >= 20, about 0 at n17
genes.author: llm:claude-fable-5-1

genes.name: multi_recreate_m
genes.hypothesis: Refills tried per ruin when multi_recreate is on (stops early once a refill beats the pre-ruin set); more refills amortise the ruin better but cost tentative evaluations.
genes.author: llm:claude-fable-5-1
